purpose: Read the PTMlink release: pairs of an N-linked glycosylation site and a phosphorylation site ranked by their co-variation across the release's CPTAC tumor cohorts (ptm_cohorts() lists them; normal adjacent tissue (NAT) cohorts are view-only and never pooled), with perturbation evidence, identifiers, a per-cohort breakdown and the reading rules on every reported pair. The package does not refit the underlying tumor associations; it calculates interval summaries and list statistics. NAT estimates and cohort-against-background comparisons are website features, outside the current pair response.

release_contract.ranking: Evidence (-log10 P) is the only sort key. Under inference_revision student_normal_bh it combines signed Student-to-normal cohort scores; earlier internal builds without the marker used Fisher-normal evidence. The pooled rho remains a Fisher-weighted effect. Sensitivity estimates are annotations, not alternate rankings.
release_contract.direction: The correlation is symmetric. No row, edge or rule licenses a direction; direction can come only from a designed perturbation.
release_contract.perturbation: Perturbation evidence admits a pair to the reported pairs and never enters the score.
release_contract.default_view: Same-protein pairs hidden; at least two cohorts; q_value < 0.05 (Benjamini-Hochberg, the only correction). To read the whole reported tier (q_value < 0.05 or perturbation evidence), set significant_only=FALSE, min_k=1 and include_cis=TRUE, with other filters reset.
release_contract.data_sources: Per-gene shards (a local web/data directory or checksum-verified download) for one gene, site or pair at a time; the released site_served.parquet (a local release directory) for questions over every reported pair.
release_contract.precision: Numbers in the shards are rounded to six decimals (q and p to seven significant digits; self_* to three decimals); the Parquet carries full precision.
release_contract.inference: Read inference metadata in build.json/shards or versions.tsv: student_normal_bh uses Student tails with Benjamini-Hochberg q_value and q_value_anchored, the only correction; earlier internal builds without the marker used Fisher-normal evidence with BH. The site, glycoform and perturbation-admitted subset are separate correction families.

rules.statement: The correlation is symmetric: the row states that the two sites co-vary across tumors, not that one regulates the other.
Significant: q < 0.05 after Benjamini-Hochberg correction over every scored site pair, the only correction applied.

Admitted by a perturbation study. Dose-response measured the pair together; gene editing and sialidase paired two lists of responding sites. Perturbation evidence admits a pair and never raises its rank.

Both sites sit on one protein and share its abundance, so they correlate under no coupling at all; same-protein pairs reach significance about ten times as often as cross-protein pairs. Read as shared abundance first.
The two parent proteins co-vary in abundance; proteins that rise and fall together make their sites co-vary for reasons outside the sites.
One side follows its own protein's abundance: an abundance observation before a site observation.
Both sites carry a tissue-program label (their intensities track a tissue-composition score), so the pair can co-vary through tissue composition alone.
Evidence grows with the number of tumors as well as with the size of the correlation; compare pairs at the same cohort count through evidence_pctile_k.
The cohorts disagree beyond sampling noise: the pooled rho is not a common effect across them (the website offers a ceiling of 0.5).
Measured in one cohort only: no heterogeneity or leave-one-cohort-out reading exists, and the default view hides such pairs.
How much of the evidence remains when the most influential cohort is left out, as a percentile among reported pairs measured in the same number of cohorts.
The composition-adjusted interval excludes zero. The adjusted score is an annotation, never a ranking, and carries no false-discovery rate.
The site-level correlation pools different representative glycoforms across cohorts; a glycan-specific statement needs the glycoform layer (ptm_pair()$glycoforms).
The glycosite's peptide carried more than one sequon; the label names the first and is an attribution, not a measurement.

functions.name: ptm_list
functions.purpose: A list of proteins or sites against the reported pairs. Auto level: protein for gene-only lists; otherwise site, with gene entries expanded to their reported sites and literal site entries preserved. Returns how each entry resolved and is covered; the pairs inside the list (internal), the same-protein pairs, and the pairs reaching out of it (neighborhood), all in the view; the ranked partner sites: sites outside the list reached by more members than their reach among all significant pairs predicts (one hypergeometric P per site, BH over every partner site; the fold; the strongest pair in the view), which answers which sites on the other side the list correlates with; the same test per partner protein (convergent); and whether the list holds more internal pairs than the members' own numbers of significant pairs predict (a degree-preserving expectation with a permutation P). The three tests count significant reported pairs (q_value < 0.05) between two different proteins; a pair reported only for its perturbation support is not counted.

tool_conventions.rows_note: Rows are sorted on evidence, the only ranking; read withheld (what the view hid, by reason) beside them and quote pair_id, never a row number.
tool_conventions.instructions: PTMlink ranks pairs of one N-glycosylation site and one phosphorylation site by the evidence that they co-vary across the release's CPTAC tumor cohorts, each correlation adjusted for its cohort's covariates (ptm_cohorts lists the cohorts; normal adjacent tissue (NAT) cohorts are view-only and never pooled). Read before calling: the correlation is symmetric and licenses no direction; site-pair results rank on the total score (evidence, -log10 P), and the adjusted, parent-conditioned and self-coupling columns are annotations that never sort and carry no false-discovery rate; perturbation evidence admits a pair and never raises its rank; the default view hides same-protein pairs, single-cohort pairs and pairs that are not significant at q < 0.05 (to see all three classes, set significant_only to false, min_k to 1 and include_cis to true, with other filters reset) and reports what it withheld. Call ptm_status first to learn how a symbol resolves and why a gene returns what it returns. Use ptm_explain to read the rules on a pair before stating anything about it. Quote pair_id, not row numbers, and cite the release from provenance. Read inference metadata: student_normal_bh uses Student tails and Benjamini-Hochberg q_value, the only correction; releases without the marker use Fisher-normal evidence with BH. List enrichment tables use their own statistics and count significant pairs (q < 0.05) between two different proteins only; their hypergeometric BH q values are a separate family. NAT estimates and cohort-against-background comparisons are website features, not returned by ptm_pair. The perturbation-subset q value is a separate family and changes neither the primary q value nor ranking.
